## Purpose
The Settings page API. It covers every configurable value of both the backend and the Tool Service, checked against the Mistral model catalog, plus the small public config that the UI reads.

## Responsibilities
- **`GET /settings`** returns `_payload()`:
  - the backend store's export sections, plus the Tool Service's sections when it is reachable;
  - every model setting gets `model_status` per model, from `catalog.model_status`;
  - `tool_service{reachable, error, url}`;
  - `catalog` meta: fetched_at, source, model_count, error, error_at, refresh_hours;
  - `restart_pending`.
- **`PUT /settings`** takes `{backend: {...}, tool_service: {...}}`:
  - it updates the backend store, then the Tool Service;
  - if the Tool Service half fails, it rolls the backend half back to the previous overrides, so one save never leaves the two services half applied;
  - a `ValueError` becomes 400 and other errors become 502 "Tool Service: …";
  - it returns `{changed: {backend, tool_service}, ...payload}`.
- **`POST /settings/reset`** takes `{target?: backend|tool_service, section?, keys?}`. If the Tool Service fails while both targets were requested, it is skipped with a warning; if only `tool_service` was requested, the failure becomes 502.
- **`GET /settings/models/catalog`** returns the catalog meta plus the models.
- **`POST /settings/models/refresh`** calls `catalog.refresh()`; a failure becomes 502 "Could not read models from Mistral: …".
- **`POST /settings/models/review?apply=`** calls `catalog.review(apply)`.
- **`GET /settings/public`** returns:
  - `models`: default_agent_model, chat_default_model, orchestrator_model, the large/medium/small tiers, `choices[{value,label}]` and `catalog`, the full model list with id, aliases, max_context_length, deprecation and the true capabilities;
  - `ui`: the value of every `UI_*` key;
  - the catalog meta.
  Labels turn `mistral-large-latest` into "Mistral Large (latest)".

## Key elements
`UpdateRequest`, `ResetRequest`, `_with_status`, `_catalog_meta` and `_payload`.

## Control flow
None.

## Data, state and side effects
- Writes `runtime_settings.json`, through the store.
- Writes the Tool Service's own settings over HTTP.
- Writes `model_catalog.json` on refresh.

## Configuration
Reads every setting.

## Interactions
- Route policy:
  - `GET /settings/public` is PUBLIC;
  - `GET /settings/models/catalog` is ANY;
  - `GET /settings` needs settings.view, and admins are allowed;
  - every other `/settings` route is ADMIN only.
- The frontend Settings page and `AppConfigApplier` use these routes.

## Error handling and edge cases
See Responsibilities.

## Nuances and gotchas
`/settings/public` is polled, and it is public: the login page needs the theme. It contains no secrets.

## How to rebuild this file
Implement the router with prefix `/settings` and the handlers described above.

## Tests
`backend/tests/test_app_settings.py`.
